name: Cham palm cake
summary: Bánh bò Chăm is the cake Vietnam Tourism tells you to watch for in Châu Đốc: soft, with a light crisp crust, made with palm sugar and coconut milk. Each cake is cooked under a hot clay lid and eaten warm. The province’s Cham-village article does not repeat the name.
origin: The Châu Đốc charms chapter on Vietnam Tourism. One source for the clay-lid method.
texture: Vietnam Tourism says the cake is soft yet crispy, and best warm, straight from the fire.
howToEat: Eat it warm, soon after it leaves the lid.
Look for it when you are in the Cham villages. A shop, an hour, and a price were not printed. Check on arrival.
where: Châu Phong and the Cham villages on the Hậu, the visit the charms chapter is sending you on. A stall was not named.
seoTitle: Banh bo Cham in Chau Doc
seoDescription: Bánh bò Chăm is a soft, lightly crisp palm-sugar cake cooked under a hot clay lid. Vietnam Tourism says eat it warm in Châu Đốc. Check on arrival.
